components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 健 is a strong body.
建 (jiàn) sounds exactly like 健; also in 键 jiàn.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 我每天下班后都会去健身房健身。
example.pinyin: wǒ měitiān xiàbān hòu dōu huì qù jiànshēnfáng jiànshēn.
example.english: I go to the gym to work out every day after work.
example.fact: Skeletal muscle is one of the few tissues that can meaningfully regenerate throughout adult life: resistance exercise triggers satellite cells at the edges of muscle fibers to fuse in and repair micro-tears. That repair process is part of why hypertrophy training requires rest days as much as effort.

examples.hanzi: 健身对身体很有好处。
examples.pinyin: Jiànshēn duì shēntǐ hěn yǒu hǎochù.
examples.english: Working out is very good for your body.

examples.hanzi: 你多久健身一次？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ duō jiǔ jiànshēn yí cì?
examples.english: How often do you work out?

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 依 is to lean on someone.
衣 (yī) — same sound — 依 is yī, like 衣.

example.hanzi: 我们要依法办事。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yī fǎ bàn shì.
example.english: We must handle matters in accordance with the law.
example.fact: 依 is the more formal, written cousin of 按 (according to): 依法 (in accordance with the law), 依据 (basis). As "to rely on," it appears in 依靠, 依赖 and 依依不舍 (reluctant to part); 依然 means "still."

examples.hanzi: 孩子很依赖父母。
examples.pinyin: Háizi hěn yīlài fùmǔ.
examples.english: The child depends heavily on his parents.

examples.hanzi: 依我看,这个办法不错。
examples.pinyin: Yī wǒ kàn, zhège bànfǎ búcuò.
examples.english: In my opinion, this method is pretty good.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — marks feelings and mood, as in 怕 fear, 快 happy, 恨 hate; 恤 is feeling pity, as in 体恤 and 抚恤.
血 (xuè) — loose sound hint (xù vs xuè).

example.hanzi: 老师很体恤学生。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī hěn tǐxù xuésheng.
example.english: The teacher is very considerate toward her students.
example.fact: 恤 means to feel for and help others: 体恤 (to empathize) and 抚恤金 (a pension for bereaved families). Most people see it in T恤, the standard Chinese for T-shirt, where it was chosen purely for its sound.

examples.hanzi: 他很体恤员工,常常关心他们。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn tǐxù yuángōng, chángcháng guānxīn tāmen.
examples.english: He is considerate of his employees and often cares about them.

examples.hanzi: 政府抚恤了受灾的家庭。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ fǔxù le shòuzāi de jiātíng.
examples.english: The government gave relief to the families hit by the disaster.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑, 驶; 驾 is to harness a horse, then drive.
加 (jiā) — same sound, different tone — 驾 is jià; 加 also sounds out 架 jià.

example.hanzi: 他刚拿到驾照，开车很小心。
example.pinyin: Tā gāng ná dào jiàzhào, kāichē hěn xiǎoxīn.
example.english: He just got his driver's license and drives very carefully.
example.fact: 驾 was about harnessing horses to a cart, and today covers all kinds of driving: 驾驶, 驾照. It also gives honorific words: 劳驾 (excuse me, may I trouble you) and 大驾光临 (your esteemed presence).

examples.hanzi: 他驾车去了机场。
examples.pinyin: Tā jià chē qù le jīchǎng.
examples.english: He drove to the airport.

examples.hanzi: 你有驾驶证吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu jiàshǐzhèng ma?
examples.english: Do you have a driver's license?

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 水和油放在一起,过一会儿就会自然分离。
example.pinyin: shuǐ hé yóu fàng zài yīqǐ, guò yīhuǐr jiù huì zìrán fēnlí.
example.english: When water and oil are put together, they naturally separate after a while.
example.fact: Water and oil separate because water molecules are polar and strongly attract each other through hydrogen bonds, squeezing out nonpolar oil molecules that can't compete for the bonding. Industrial oil-spill skimmers exploit this same principle to draw crude oil off the surface of seawater.

examples.hanzi: 孩子和父母分离了好几年。
examples.pinyin: Háizi hé fùmǔ fēnlí le hǎo jǐ nián.
examples.english: The child was separated from his parents for several years.

examples.hanzi: 这个实验需要把两种液体分离。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shíyàn xūyào bǎ liǎng zhǒng yètǐ fēnlí.
examples.english: This experiment requires separating the two liquids.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 小偷是从后门溜进屋子的。
example.pinyin: xiǎotōu shì cóng hòumén liū jìn wūzi de.
example.english: The thief slipped into the house through the back door.
example.fact: In 2010, security researchers discovered that the Stuxnet worm exploited a legitimate but undocumented backdoor in Siemens industrial control software to sabotage centrifuges at Iran's Natanz nuclear facility — one of the first cyberweapons known to cause physical damage to critical infrastructure.

examples.hanzi: 后门没锁，你可以直接进来。
examples.pinyin: Hòumén méi suǒ, nǐ kěyǐ zhíjiē jìnlái.
examples.english: The back door isn't locked, so you can come right in.

examples.hanzi: 他想走后门找份好工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zǒu hòumén zhǎo fèn hǎo gōngzuò.
examples.english: He wants to use connections to get a good job.

components.note: 戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; here part of the simplified form 胜 for victory.
生 (shēng) is a near sound match for shèng; also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 中国女排在决赛中战胜了强劲的对手。
example.pinyin: zhōngguó nǚpái zài juésài zhōng zhànshèngle qiángjìng de duìshǒu.
example.english: The Chinese women's volleyball team defeated a strong opponent in the final.
example.fact: In the 1980 Winter Olympics 'Miracle on Ice,' a team of American college and amateur players defeated the heavily favored Soviet squad, which had won gold in five of the previous six Olympics — one of the most celebrated upsets in sports history.

examples.hanzi: 我们一定能战胜这场疾病。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yídìng néng zhànshèng zhè chǎng jíbìng.
examples.english: We will certainly overcome this illness.

examples.hanzi: 他终于战胜了自己的恐惧。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú zhànshèng le zìjǐ de kǒngjù.
examples.english: He finally conquered his own fear.

components.note: 亻 (person) — Buddha is a person; the same part marks people, as in 仙 immortal, 你 you.
弗 (fú) gives the sound as in 仿佛 fǎng fú; it also sounds out 费 fèi and 拂 fú.
罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.

example.hanzi: 他们计划下个月去佛罗里达度假。
example.pinyin: tāmen jìhuà xià gè yuè qù Fóluólǐdá dùjià.
example.english: They plan to vacation in Florida next month.
example.fact: NASA deliberately built the Kennedy Space Center on Florida's Atlantic coast in the 1960s partly because launching rockets eastward near the equator lets them borrow extra speed from Earth's own rotation, saving fuel that a launch from a site farther north would have to burn instead.

examples.hanzi: 佛罗里达的冬天很暖和。
examples.pinyin: Fóluólǐdá de dōngtiān hěn nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: Winters in Florida are very warm.

examples.hanzi: 我表姐住在佛罗里达。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ biǎojiě zhù zài Fóluólǐdá.
examples.english: My cousin lives in Florida.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person falling over; marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做.
到 (dào) gives the sound: 倒 is dǎo (fall) or dào (upside down).
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 那棵老树在暴风雨中轰然倒下。
example.pinyin: nà kē lǎoshù zài bàofēngyǔ zhōng hōngrán dǎoxià.
example.english: The old tree collapsed with a crash in the storm.
example.fact: Redwood trees can weigh over 1,000 tons and grow past 100 meters tall, yet their root systems rarely extend more than 3-4 meters deep. They survive storms largely by spreading their roots wide and intertwining them with neighboring redwoods, effectively holding each other up underground.

examples.hanzi: 他累得一进门就倒下了。
examples.pinyin: Tā lèi de yí jìnmén jiù dǎoxià le.
examples.english: He was so tired that he collapsed as soon as he came in.

examples.hanzi: 墙在大风中倒下了。
examples.pinyin: Qiáng zài dàfēng zhōng dǎoxià le.
examples.english: The wall fell over in the strong wind.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — plain unmixed thread, hence pure; also in 红 red, 级 level.
屯 (tún) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 钝 dùn and 顿 dùn.

example.hanzi: 这杯果汁是纯的，没加糖。
example.pinyin: Zhè bēi guǒzhī shì chún de, méi jiā táng.
example.english: This juice is pure, with no added sugar.
example.fact: 纯 describes something unmixed: 纯棉 (pure cotton, seen on clothing labels), 纯净水 (purified water), 单纯 (simple, naive), 纯洁 (pure). 纯属 means "purely" and is used to deny things: 纯属误会 (a pure misunderstanding).

examples.hanzi: 这是一种纯天然的蜂蜜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng chún tiānrán de fēngmì.
examples.english: This is a kind of pure natural honey.

examples.hanzi: 她是个单纯的女孩。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge dānchún de nǚhái.
examples.english: She is a simple, innocent girl.

components.note: 木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.
氵 (water) — marks liquids; 汁 is juice or sap, as in 汤 soup, 酒 liquor.
十 (shí) is only a loose sound clue for zhī.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每天早上都会榨新鲜的果汁给我喝。
example.pinyin: māma měitiān zǎoshang dōu huì zhà xīnxiān de guǒzhī gěi wǒ hē.
example.english: Mom squeezes fresh fruit juice for me to drink every morning.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials, discovering that citrus fruit cured scurvy among sailors — decades before vitamin C was even identified, in 1932, as the compound actually responsible.

examples.hanzi: 请给我一杯橙子果汁。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi chéngzi guǒzhī.
examples.english: Please give me a glass of orange juice.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子不应该喝太多果汁。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi bù yīnggāi hē tài duō guǒzhī.
examples.english: Kids shouldn't drink too much fruit juice.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 被 is a quilt, then the passive marker.
皮 (pí) — loose hint — 被 is bèi; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī and 坡 pō.
辶 (movement) — marks walking, roads and motion, as in 过 pass, 进 enter, 追 chase; 迫 is to press or drive someone on.
白 (bái) is a loose hint for pò; 拍 pāi and 泊 bó share the same part.

example.hanzi: 由于资金短缺,公司被迫裁员。
example.pinyin: yóuyú zījīn duǎnquē, gōngsī bèipò cáiyuán.
example.english: Due to a funding shortage, the company was forced to lay off staff.
example.fact: When Krakatoa erupted in 1883, the blast was heard over 3,000 miles away in Mauritius, and life on the devastated island was forced to restart from almost nothing. The very first colonizers to reach the sterilized island were spiders, arriving on wind-blown silk within months of the eruption.

examples.hanzi: 他被迫放弃了这次机会。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèipò fàngqì le zhè cì jīhuì.
examples.english: He was forced to give up this opportunity.

examples.hanzi: 大雪让航班被迫取消。
examples.pinyin: Dàxuě ràng hángbān bèipò qǔxiāo.
examples.english: The heavy snow forced the flight to be cancelled.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 披 is draping over the shoulders, as in 披风.
皮 (pí) — close sound: 披 pī. 皮 also sounds out 被 bèi and 疲 pí.

example.hanzi: 她在肩上披了一件外套。
example.pinyin: Tā zài jiān shàng pī le yí jiàn wàitào.
example.english: She draped a coat over her shoulders.
example.fact: 披 means to throw something loosely over your shoulders without putting arms in the sleeves: 披肩 (shawl), 披头散发 (hair hanging loose). It also means to reveal, as in 披露, and is the first syllable of 披萨 (pizza).

examples.hanzi: 他披上外套出门了。
examples.pinyin: Tā pī shàng wàitào chūmén le.
examples.english: He threw on his coat and went out.

examples.hanzi: 她披着长长的头发。
examples.pinyin: Tā pī zhe chángcháng de tóufa.
examples.english: She has long hair draped over her shoulders.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 渣 is what is left after liquid is strained, as in 残渣.
查 (chá) — close sound: 渣 zhā. 查 also sounds out 楂 zhā.

example.hanzi: 咖啡渣可以用来种花。
example.pinyin: Kāfēi zhā kěyǐ yòng lái zhòng huā.
example.english: Coffee grounds can be used for growing flowers.
example.fact: 渣 means leftover bits: 豆渣 (soy pulp), 煤渣 (cinders), 饼干渣 (biscuit crumbs). Online, 渣男 ("scum guy") and 渣女 are common slang terms for unfaithful or heartless partners.

examples.hanzi: 他把碗里的饭渣都吃干净了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ wǎn lǐ de fànzhā dōu chī gānjìng le.
examples.english: He finished every crumb of rice in his bowl.

examples.hanzi: 桌子上有很多面包渣。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu hěn duō miànbāozhā.
examples.english: There are a lot of bread crumbs on the table.

components.note: 毛 (hair) — a picture of a tuft of hair or fur; used in 毛巾 and 毛病 (a flaw).
巾 — a piece of cloth hanging from a line; marks cloth items, as in 布 cloth, 帽 hat, 帐 curtain.

example.hanzi: 他用毛巾擦干了头发。
example.pinyin: tā yòng máojīn cāgānle tóufǎ.
example.english: He dried his hair with a towel.
example.fact: Terry cloth towels get their absorbency from thousands of small uncut loops of cotton yarn woven into the base fabric, which dramatically increases surface area — a single terry towel can expose several times more fiber surface than a flat cotton sheet of the same size.

examples.hanzi: 这条毛巾太小了，再拿一条吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo máojīn tài xiǎo le, zài ná yì tiáo ba.
examples.english: This towel is too small, so get another one.

examples.hanzi: 游泳后请用干毛巾擦干身体。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyǒng hòu qǐng yòng gān máojīn cā gān shēntǐ.
examples.english: After swimming, please dry off with a dry towel.

meanings: the great bulk of the population

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
人 (person) — three persons 人人人: a crowd. Also in 观众 audience, 大众 the public.

example.hanzi: 这部电影深受大众喜爱。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng shēn shòu dàzhòng xǐ'ài.
example.english: This movie is deeply loved by the general public.
example.fact: Henry Ford's moving assembly line, introduced in 1913, cut the time to build a Model T chassis from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes. That efficiency let Ford slash prices repeatedly, turning the automobile from a luxury item into something the general public could actually afford.

examples.hanzi: 这是一款大众都买得起的车。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì kuǎn dàzhòng dōu mǎi de qǐ de chē.
examples.english: This is a car that ordinary people can afford.

examples.hanzi: 大众传媒影响着我们的生活。
examples.pinyin: Dàzhòng chuánmèi yǐngxiǎng zhe wǒmen de shēnghuó.
examples.english: The mass media affects our daily lives.

components.note: 犭 (dog, animal) — animals, as in 狗, 猫, 猪: a wild animal.
王 (wáng) is a loose sound clue for kuáng; 王 also in 往 wǎng and 旺 wàng.
欠 (yawn, open mouth) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow.
又 here replaces 雚 (huān) in the traditional 歡, so it is only a stand-in; same shorthand in 观 and 劝.

example.hanzi: 巴西的狂欢节吸引了来自世界各地的游客。
example.pinyin: bāxī de kuánghuānjié xīyǐnle láizì shìjiè gèdì de yóukè.
example.english: Brazil's carnival attracts tourists from all over the world.
example.fact: Rio de Janeiro's Carnival parade features samba schools competing inside a purpose-built stadium called the Sambadrome, completed in 1984. Each school gets roughly an hour to march about 700 meters while judges score costumes, choreography, and drumming in real time.

examples.hanzi: 比赛结束后，球迷们尽情狂欢。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jiéshù hòu, qiúmímen jìnqíng kuánghuān.
examples.english: After the game, the fans partied to their hearts' content.

examples.hanzi: 大家在广场上狂欢了一整夜。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā zài guǎngchǎng shàng kuánghuān le yì zhěng yè.
examples.english: Everyone celebrated in the square all night long.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 这件毛衣是奶奶亲手织的。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn máoyī shì nǎinai qīnshǒu zhī de.
example.english: This sweater was knitted by grandma with her own hands.
example.fact: A traditional hand-tied Persian carpet can contain over one million individual knots per square meter, each tied by hand. A skilled weaver working steadily might still take a full year to complete a single large rug.

examples.hanzi: 这顿饭是我亲手做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dùn fàn shì wǒ qīnshǒu zuò de.
examples.english: I cooked this meal with my own hands.

examples.hanzi: 他亲手把礼物交给了妹妹。
examples.pinyin: Tā qīnshǒu bǎ lǐwù jiāo gěi le mèimei.
examples.english: He handed the gift to his sister personally.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a quiet house; marks shelter and rooms, as in 家 home, 安 peace.
叔 (shū) is only a loose sound clue for jì.
宀 (roof) — a still, empty house; also in 家 home, 安 peace.
莫 (mò) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 墓 mù, 幕 mù, 摸 mō and 膜 mó.

example.hanzi: 退休以后,他常常感到寂寞。
example.pinyin: tuìxiū yǐhòu, tā chángcháng gǎndào jìmò.
example.english: After retiring, he often feels lonely.
example.fact: Psychologist John Cacioppo's longitudinal research found that chronic loneliness raises cortisol levels and disrupts sleep in ways comparable to physical stressors. Several large follow-up studies have since linked sustained social isolation to mortality risk on par with smoking roughly 15 cigarettes a day.

examples.hanzi: 一个人住在外地，有时会觉得寂寞。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge rén zhù zài wàidì, yǒushí huì juéde jìmò.
examples.english: Living alone in another city, you sometimes feel lonely.

examples.hanzi: 夜深了，街上显得很寂寞。
examples.pinyin: Yè shēn le, jiē shàng xiǎnde hěn jìmò.
examples.english: It was late at night and the street looked deserted.

components.note: 未 (not yet) — a tree 木 with a new short branch on top, still growing. Compare 末 mò (end/tip), where the top stroke is longer.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 她带着未婚夫回家见父母。
example.pinyin: tā dàizhe wèihūnfū huí jiā jiàn fùmǔ.
example.english: She brought her fiancé home to meet her parents.
example.fact: The tradition of a diamond engagement ring is largely a 20th-century marketing invention: De Beers' 1947 ad campaign coined the slogan 'A Diamond Is Forever,' turning what had been a relatively uncommon gift into an expected part of Western marriage proposals within a couple of decades.

examples.hanzi: 她的未婚夫是一名医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā de wèihūnfū shì yì míng yīshēng.
examples.english: Her fiancé is a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 我还没见过她的未婚夫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi jiànguo tā de wèihūnfū.
examples.english: I haven't met her fiancé yet.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 工人们正在清除路上的积雪。
example.pinyin: gōngrénmen zhèngzài qīngchú lù shàng de jīxuě.
example.english: Workers are clearing away the snow on the road.
example.fact: Japan's Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route cuts through the 'Yuki-no-Otani' snow corridor, where plows carve a road between walls of snow that can tower over 20 meters — among the tallest man-made snow canyons on Earth, cleared fresh each spring.

examples.hanzi: 请及时清除电脑里的垃圾文件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jíshí qīngchú diànnǎo lǐ de lājī wénjiàn.
examples.english: Please clear the junk files off your computer promptly.

examples.hanzi: 他想清除脸上的污渍。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qīngchú liǎn shàng de wūzì.
examples.english: He wants to remove the stains from his face.

components.note: 酋 (wine jar) with a hand 寸 offering it: honoring a guest. 尊 sounds out 遵 zūn (obey) and 樽 zūn (goblet).
厂 (cliff) — the visible frame, as in 原, 厚. Memory aid: a stern cliff face — 严重 serious, 严格 strict. Cliff family hint, not proven.
嚴 (traditional) — a larger shape with two mouths 吅 shouting orders. 严 cut it to 亚 plus 厂, losing the clue.

example.hanzi: 每个人都应该有尊严地生活。
example.pinyin: měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi yǒu zūnyán de shēnghuó.
example.english: Everyone should live with dignity.
example.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1948, opens its very first article by asserting that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights — a direct response to the atrocities of World War II.

examples.hanzi: 我们要尊重别人的尊严。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zūnzhòng biéren de zūnyán.
examples.english: We should respect other people's dignity.

examples.hanzi: 他不想为了钱而失去尊严。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng wèile qián ér shīqù zūnyán.
examples.english: He doesn't want to lose his dignity for money.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢在学校演戏。
example.pinyin: tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuān zài xuéxiào yǎnxì.
example.english: He has loved performing plays at school since childhood.
example.fact: The Theatre of Dionysus in Athens, carved into the slope of the Acropolis around the 6th century BC, could seat roughly 17,000 spectators. It's considered the birthplace of Western drama, hosting the original performances of plays by Sophocles and Euripides.

examples.hanzi: 别在我面前演戏了，我都看出来了。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài wǒ miànqián yǎnxì le, wǒ dōu kàn chūlái le.
examples.english: Stop putting on an act in front of me, I can already tell.

examples.hanzi: 这些孩子正在台上演戏。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē háizi zhèngzài tái shàng yǎnxì.
examples.english: The children are performing a play on the stage.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 手机的定位功能帮我们找到了最近的餐厅。
example.pinyin: shǒujī de dìngwèi gōngnéng bāng wǒmen zhǎodàole zuìjìn de cāntīng.
example.english: The phone's positioning function helped us find the nearest restaurant.
example.fact: GPS satellites carry atomic clocks accurate to within a few billionths of a second, but under Einstein's relativity, their onboard clocks actually run faster than clocks on Earth's surface. Engineers deliberately slow them down before launch by about 38 microseconds a day to keep positioning accurate.

examples.hanzi: 请打开手机的定位，我来找你。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dǎkāi shǒujī de dìngwèi, wǒ lái zhǎo nǐ.
examples.english: Please turn on your phone's location, and I'll come find you.

examples.hanzi: 这个品牌的定位是年轻人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège pǐnpái de dìngwèi shì niánqīngrén.
examples.english: This brand's positioning targets young people.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.

example.hanzi: 他没准明天就回来了。
example.pinyin: tā méizhǔn míngtiān jiù huílái le.
example.english: He might come back tomorrow, who knows.
example.fact: Even with supercomputers, weather forecasts lose most of their reliability beyond about two weeks — a consequence of chaos theory's 'butterfly effect,' first modeled by meteorologist Edward Lorenz in 1961 when rounding a variable to three decimal places instead of six produced a wildly different simulated forecast.

examples.hanzi: 没准他已经到家了。
examples.pinyin: Méizhǔn tā yǐjīng dào jiā le.
examples.english: He may well already be home.

examples.hanzi: 你先带把伞吧，没准会下雨。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān dài bǎ sǎn ba, méizhǔn huì xiàyǔ.
examples.english: Take an umbrella just in case, it might rain.

components.note: 艹 (grass, 草字头) — marks plants; 芯 is a plant's pith or core, as in 花 flower, 草 grass.
心 (xīn, heart) gives the exact sound and the idea: the heart of the plant, as in 灯芯 lamp wick.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 这款手机使用了最新的芯片。
example.pinyin: zhè kuǎn shǒujī shǐyòngle zuìxīn de xīnpiàn.
example.english: This phone uses the latest chip.
example.fact: In 1965, Intel co-founder Gordon Moore observed that the number of transistors on an integrated circuit was doubling roughly every two years — a prediction now known as Moore's Law that held remarkably well for over five decades before physical limits began to slow it in the 2020s.

examples.hanzi: 这台电脑的芯片很先进。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo de xīnpiàn hěn xiānjìn.
examples.english: This computer's chip is very advanced.

examples.hanzi: 工厂正在生产新型芯片。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng zhèngzài shēngchǎn xīnxíng xīnpiàn.
examples.english: The factory is producing a new type of chip.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 核 is a fruit stone or kernel; 木 marks trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 桌 table.
亥 (hài) is a loose sound clue; it also sounds out 孩 hái, 咳 ké and 刻 kè.
弓 (bow) — bows and tension: 张 stretch, 引 draw, 弯 bend; 弹 is to shoot or spring, and a bullet.
单 (dān) is a loose clue for dàn/tán; compare 禅 chán and 蝉 chán.

example.hanzi: 这部纪录片讲述了核弹研发的历史。
example.pinyin: zhè bù jìlùpiàn jiǎngshùle hédàn yánfā de lìshǐ.
example.english: This documentary tells the history of nuclear bomb development.
example.fact: The largest nuclear weapon ever detonated, the Soviet 'Tsar Bomba' tested in 1961 over Novaya Zemlya, released roughly 3,300 times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb. Its shockwave reportedly broke windows in Norway and Finland, over 500 miles away.

examples.hanzi: 核弹的威力非常巨大。
examples.pinyin: Hédàn de wēilì fēicháng jùdà.
examples.english: The power of a nuclear bomb is enormous.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆里展出了一枚核弹模型。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchū le yì méi hédàn móxíng.
examples.english: A model of a nuclear bomb is on display in the museum.

meanings: unit (group of people as a whole)

components.note: 单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 他所在的单位负责这个项目的管理。
example.pinyin: tā suǒzài de dānwèi fùzé zhège xiàngmù de guǎnlǐ.
example.english: The organization he works for is responsible for managing this project.
example.fact: In 2019, the kilogram — the last SI base unit still defined by a physical object, a platinum-iridium cylinder locked in a Paris vault since 1889 — was redefined in terms of the Planck constant, finally freeing the entire metric system from dependence on a single physical artifact.

examples.hanzi: 请填写你的姓名和工作单位。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tiánxiě nǐ de xìngmíng hé gōngzuò dānwèi.
examples.english: Please fill in your name and place of work.

examples.hanzi: 米是长度的单位。
examples.pinyin: Mǐ shì chángdù de dānwèi.
examples.english: The meter is a unit of length.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 for cloth and wearables, as in 布, 帐, 带; 帽 is a cloth head covering.
冒 (mào) — same sound — 帽 is mào, matching 冒.

example.hanzi: 天气冷，你戴上帽子吧。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì lěng, nǐ dàishang màozi ba.
example.english: It is cold, so put on a hat.
example.fact: 帽 is normally paired as 帽子, with the measure word 顶: 一顶帽子. You 戴 (wear) a hat. Figuratively, 扣帽子 means to slap a label on someone, and 高帽子 means flattery.

examples.hanzi: 你的帽子真好看，在哪儿买的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de màozi zhēn hǎokàn, zài nǎr mǎi de?
examples.english: Your hat is so nice. Where did you buy it?

examples.hanzi: 他进门以后摘下了帽子。
examples.pinyin: Tā jìn mén yǐhòu zhāi xià le màozi.
examples.english: He took off his hat after coming in.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 爷爷喜欢每天早上听收音机里的新闻。
example.pinyin: yéye xǐhuān měitiān zǎoshang tīng shōuyīnjī lǐ de xīnwén.
example.english: Grandpa likes listening to the news on the radio every morning.
example.fact: In 1920, Pittsburgh station KDKA broadcast the results of the Harding-Cox presidential election, one of the first scheduled commercial radio broadcasts in the U.S. Within just a few years, radio ownership exploded from a hobbyist niche into a fixture of millions of American homes.

examples.hanzi: 这台旧收音机还能用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái jiù shōuyīnjī hái néng yòng.
examples.english: This old radio still works.

examples.hanzi: 开车的时候他喜欢听收音机。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē de shíhou tā xǐhuan tīng shōuyīnjī.
examples.english: He likes listening to the radio while driving.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metal restraints; also in 钱 money, 铁 iron.
考 (kǎo) is the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 烤 kǎo and 拷 kǎo.

example.hanzi: 警察给逃跑的嫌疑人戴上了手铐。
example.pinyin: jǐngchá gěi táopǎo de xiányírén dàishàngle shǒukào.
example.english: The police put handcuffs on the fleeing suspect.
example.fact: Harry Houdini built much of his early fame on escaping police handcuffs and jail cells in the early 1900s, often asking local officers to search and lock him up in each city he visited as a publicity stunt meant to prove no restraint could hold him.

examples.hanzi: 警察用手铐铐住了他的双手。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá yòng shǒukào kào zhù le tā de shuāngshǒu.
examples.english: The police cuffed his hands with handcuffs.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的小偷戴着手铐被带走了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de xiǎotōu dàizhe shǒukào bèi dàizǒu le.
examples.english: In the movie, the thief was led away in handcuffs.

components.note: 白 (bái) hints at the sound: 百 bǎi is close, and 白 also gives 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.
耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 湖; 汇 is waters flowing together.
匚 (box) — the container the water gathers in, as in 区.

example.hanzi: 这部音乐剧在百老汇上演了整整十年。
example.pinyin: zhè bù yīnyuèjù zài Bǎilǎohuì shàngyǎnle zhěngzhěng shí nián.
example.english: This musical has run on Broadway for a full ten years.
example.fact: Broadway's longest-running show, The Phantom of the Opera, opened in 1988 and played for 35 consecutive years before closing in 2023. Over that run it employed an estimated 6,500 people and grossed more revenue than any other production in theater history.

examples.hanzi: 我想去纽约的百老汇看演出。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Niǔyuē de Bǎilǎohuì kàn yǎnchū.
examples.english: I want to see a show on Broadway in New York.

examples.hanzi: 百老汇的剧院总是座无虚席。
examples.pinyin: Bǎilǎohuì de jùyuàn zǒngshì zuò wú xū xí.
examples.english: The theaters on Broadway are always packed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 士兵们在恶劣的天气中继续作战。
example.pinyin: shìbīngmen zài èliè de tiānqì zhōng jìxù zuòzhàn.
example.english: The soldiers continued fighting in the harsh weather.
example.fact: During the WWII Battle of Stalingrad, winter temperatures fell below -30°C. German troops, left with only summer uniforms after Hitler expected a quick victory, suffered tens of thousands of frostbite casualties before the battle ended in February 1943.

examples.hanzi: 两支队伍在山区作战。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhī duìwu zài shānqū zuòzhàn.
examples.english: The two armies are fighting in the mountains.

examples.hanzi: 团队合作比单独作战更有效。
examples.pinyin: Tuánduì hézuò bǐ dāndú zuòzhàn gèng yǒuxiào.
examples.english: Teamwork is more effective than fighting alone.

meanings: to discuss a paper or thesis

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.
文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.

example.hanzi: 她正在图书馆里写毕业论文。
example.pinyin: tā zhèngzài túshūguǎn lǐ xiě bìyè lùnwén.
example.english: She is writing her graduation thesis in the library.
example.fact: The modern practice of peer review is often traced to the Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions in the 1660s, though it didn't become standard scientific practice until the 20th century — before then, journal editors alone typically decided what to publish.

examples.hanzi: 老师要求我们下周交论文。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yāoqiú wǒmen xià zhōu jiāo lùnwén.
examples.english: The teacher wants us to hand in our papers next week.

examples.hanzi: 这篇论文讨论了环境污染的问题。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān lùnwén tǎolùn le huánjìng wūrǎn de wèntí.
examples.english: This paper discusses the problem of environmental pollution.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 遗 is leaving something behind or losing it.
贵 (valuable) — what is precious is what you regret leaving behind or what is left to heirs.
口 (mouth) — speaking instructions; also in 叫 shout, 问 ask.
属 (shǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 瞩 zhǔ, as in 嘱咐.

example.hanzi: 老人在去世前立下了一份遗嘱。
example.pinyin: lǎorén zài qùshì qián lìxiàle yī fèn yízhǔ.
example.english: The elderly person made a will before passing away.
example.fact: The oldest surviving will in the world is believed to belong to an Egyptian priest named Wah, written around 1800 BC on papyrus and discovered at the site of Thebes. It names his mother as the sole heir to his property.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷的遗嘱放在抽屉里。
examples.pinyin: Yéye de yízhǔ fàng zài chōuti lǐ.
examples.english: Grandpa's will is kept in the drawer.

examples.hanzi: 他请律师帮忙写遗嘱。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐng lǜshī bāngmáng xiě yízhǔ.
examples.english: He asked a lawyer to help him write a will.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.

example.hanzi: 战争给平民带来了巨大的痛苦。
example.pinyin: zhànzhēng gěi píngmín dàiláile jùdà de tòngkǔ.
example.english: War brought enormous suffering to civilians.
example.fact: The Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949 was the first international treaty to focus specifically on protecting civilians in wartime, drafted in direct response to the widespread targeting of noncombatant populations during World War II.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的价格对平民来说很合适。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de jiàgé duì píngmín lái shuō hěn héshì.
examples.english: This restaurant's prices are reasonable for ordinary people.

examples.hanzi: 他出身平民家庭，靠努力考上了大学。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūshēn píngmín jiātíng, kào nǔlì kǎoshàng le dàxué.
examples.english: He came from an ordinary family and got into university through hard work.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 这本书的作者是一位年轻的女作家。
example.pinyin: zhè běn shū de zuòzhě shì yī wèi niánqīng de nǚ zuòjiā.
example.english: The author of this book is a young female writer.
example.fact: The identity of Elena Ferrante, author of the internationally acclaimed Neapolitan Novels, remains disputed and unconfirmed to the public. Despite investigative attempts, including a controversial 2016 financial-document analysis, the author has never publicly confirmed a name.

examples.hanzi: 这位作者的新书下个月出版。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòzhě de xīn shū xià ge yuè chūbǎn.
examples.english: This author's new book comes out next month.

examples.hanzi: 你知道这首歌的作者是谁吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào zhè shǒu gē de zuòzhě shì shéi ma?
examples.english: Do you know who the author of this song is?

components.note: 韦 (leather; from 韋) — the right half. 韩 is mainly a name today (Korea, surname Han); the parts no longer explain the meaning.
龺 (sunrays over a pole) — the left part, the same as in 乾 and 朝. Memory aid: just a visual block; say 'hán' by its look, not by its parts.

example.hanzi: 她想去韩国旅游。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù Hánguó lǚyóu.
example.english: She wants to travel to South Korea.
example.fact: In modern usage 韩 stands for Korea (韩国 South Korea, 韩语 Korean, 韩剧 K-drama). It is the same character as the ancient Chinese state of Han and the surname, but the Korean name 한 simply happens to be written with it.

examples.hanzi: 我的同学是韩国人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngxué shì Hánguó rén.
examples.english: My classmate is Korean.

examples.hanzi: 她很喜欢看韩剧。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan kàn Hánjù.
examples.english: She really likes watching Korean dramas.

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
亏 is the simplified form of 虧, whose 虍 (tiger) part was dropped; the leftover shape no longer shows the meaning. Memory aid: it looks like 于 with a hook — 'cut short, a loss'.

example.hanzi: 多亏了邻居的帮助,我们才顺利搬完家。
example.pinyin: duōkuī le línjū de bāngzhù, wǒmen cái shùnlì bān wán jiā.
example.english: Thanks to the neighbor's help, we finished moving smoothly.
example.fact: Vampire bats are one of the few mammals known to regularly share regurgitated blood with roost-mates who failed to feed that night. Researchers have found the bats preferentially help individuals who have helped them before — a rare documented case of reciprocal altruism in the wild.

examples.hanzi: 多亏你提醒我，不然我就忘了。
examples.pinyin: Duōkuī nǐ tíxǐng wǒ, bùrán wǒ jiù wàng le.
examples.english: Thanks to your reminder, I would have forgotten otherwise.

examples.hanzi: 多亏带了伞，我们才没被淋湿。
examples.pinyin: Duōkuī dài le sǎn, wǒmen cái méi bèi línshī.
examples.english: Luckily we brought an umbrella, so we didn't get soaked.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).

example.hanzi: 医生建议他控制体重,多运动。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiànyì tā kòngzhì tǐzhòng, duō yùndòng.
example.english: The doctor advised him to control his body weight and exercise more.
example.fact: Astronauts don't lose actual mass by going into orbit — they float because they and their spacecraft are in continuous free fall around Earth, not because gravity has vanished. At the International Space Station's altitude, Earth's gravity is still about 90% as strong as at the surface.

examples.hanzi: 我最近体重增加了三公斤。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn tǐzhòng zēngjiā le sān gōngjīn.
examples.english: My weight has gone up three kilograms recently.

examples.hanzi: 你每天都称体重吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ měi tiān dōu chēng tǐzhòng ma?
examples.english: Do you weigh yourself every day?

components.note: 向 (toward) — a window 口 in a wall facing a direction, hence toward. It also gives its sound to 响 xiǎng and 饷 xiǎng.
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.hanzi: 遇到困难时,我们要勇敢地向前。
example.pinyin: yùdào kùnnán shí, wǒmen yào yǒnggǎn de xiàngqián.
example.english: When facing difficulties, we should bravely move forward.
example.fact: Sea horses are the only fish known to swim upright, propelling themselves forward almost entirely with a dorsal fin that beats up to 30 times per second. That swimming style is so inefficient that sea horses are also among the slowest-moving fish in the ocean.

examples.hanzi: 请向前走五十米，然后右转。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiàng qián zǒu wǔshí mǐ, ránhòu yòu zhuǎn.
examples.english: Please walk forward fifty meters and then turn right.

examples.hanzi: 我们要看着未来，继续向前。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào kànzhe wèilái, jìxù xiàng qián.
examples.english: We should look to the future and keep moving forward.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 伴 is a companion, as in 伙伴.
半 (bàn) — same sound — 伴 is bàn, like 半; 半 also sounds out 拌 bàn and 叛 pàn.
亻 (person) — companions are people; also in 他 he, 伴 partner.
吕 (lǚ) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 铝 lǚ (aluminium).

example.hanzi: 他们是相识多年的老伴侣。
example.pinyin: tāmen shì xiāngshí duōnián de lǎo bànlǚ.
example.english: They are longtime companions who have known each other for years.
example.fact: Albatrosses often mate with the same partner for decades and perform elaborate, synchronized courtship dances that can take years to perfect. Some individuals return to the same mate at the same nesting site every breeding season for over 50 years.

examples.hanzi: 他们是一对幸福的伴侣。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yí duì xìngfú de bànlǚ.
examples.english: They are a happy couple.

examples.hanzi: 狗是很多老人的伴侣。
examples.pinyin: Gǒu shì hěn duō lǎorén de bànlǚ.
examples.english: For many elderly people, a dog is a companion.

components.note: 巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.
西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.

example.hanzi: 巴西是世界上咖啡产量最大的国家。
example.pinyin: Bāxī shì shìjiè shàng kāfēi chǎnliàng zuìdà de guójiā.
example.english: Brazil is the world's largest coffee-producing country.
example.fact: Brazil produces roughly a third of the world's coffee supply, a dominance traceable to seedlings smuggled out of French Guiana in 1727. Legend holds that a Portuguese officer received them as a farewell gift from the French governor's wife, planting the seeds that grew into Brazil's coffee industry today.

examples.hanzi: 我明年想去巴西看足球比赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngnián xiǎng qù Bāxī kàn zúqiú bǐsài.
examples.english: Next year I want to go to Brazil to watch a soccer match.

examples.hanzi: 他在巴西住了三年，会说葡萄牙语。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Bāxī zhù le sān nián, huì shuō Pútáoyáyǔ.
examples.english: He lived in Brazil for three years and speaks Portuguese.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 她心里有一种不祥的预感。
example.pinyin: tā xīnlǐ yǒu yī zhǒng bùxiáng de yùgǎn.
example.english: She had an ominous premonition in her heart.
example.fact: Some animals, including catfish and toads, have been observed behaving unusually in the hours before earthquakes, but decades of research have failed to establish a reliable biological early-warning signal. Most scientists attribute reported cases to coincidence or to subtle ground vibrations animals sense just seconds before humans do.

examples.hanzi: 我有一种不好的预感。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yì zhǒng bù hǎo de yùgǎn.
examples.english: I have a bad feeling about this.

examples.hanzi: 他预感到这次考试会很难。
examples.pinyin: Tā yùgǎn dào zhè cì kǎoshì huì hěn nán.
examples.english: He had a premonition that this exam would be hard.

components.note: 色 (colour, beauty) — the colour part; 艳 means vividly beautiful: 艳丽 gorgeous, 鲜艳 bright. The traditional form is 艷.
丰 (abundant) — the left part: a rich, full look. Together: richly colourful, glamorous.

example.hanzi: 院子里的花开得很艳。
example.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ de huā kāi de hěn yàn.
example.english: The flowers in the yard are blooming brilliantly.
example.fact: 艳 describes vivid, rich colour: 鲜艳 (brightly coloured), 艳丽 (gorgeous), 艳阳天 (a bright, sunny day). 艳遇 means a romantic encounter, and 艳 is often attached to flowers or dresses.

examples.hanzi: 她穿了一条很艳的红裙子。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān le yì tiáo hěn yàn de hóng qúnzi.
examples.english: She wore a vivid red skirt.

examples.hanzi: 春天来了，到处都是鲜艳的花。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān lái le, dàochù dōu shì xiānyàn de huā.
examples.english: Spring has come, and there are bright flowers everywhere.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a walled-in border; 固 is something fenced in and firm, as in 国 country, 围 surround.
古 (gǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 故 gù, 姑 gū and 苦 kǔ.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 书架已经固定在墙上了。
example.pinyin: shūjià yǐjīng gùdìng zài qiáng shàng le.
example.english: The bookshelf has already been fixed to the wall.
example.fact: Ancient astronomers called stars 'fixed' because, unlike the planets (from the Greek for 'wanderers'), they appeared to hold constant positions relative to each other. It wasn't until the 18th century that astronomer Edmund Halley confirmed stars actually do move, just too slowly and too far away for the shift to be visible within a human lifetime.

examples.hanzi: 我们的上班时间是固定的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de shàngbān shíjiān shì gùdìng de.
examples.english: Our working hours are fixed.

examples.hanzi: 请把桌子固定好，不要让它晃动。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi gùdìng hǎo, bú yào ràng tā huàngdòng.
examples.english: Please secure the table so that it doesn't wobble.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.
口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.

example.hanzi: 每个地方的口味都不太一样。
example.pinyin: měi gè dìfang de kǒuwèi dōu bù tài yīyàng.
example.english: The taste preferences are somewhat different in every place.
example.fact: Humans have roughly 10,000 taste buds distributed not just on the tongue but also on the soft palate, throat, and even the epiglottis. Each bud is replaced about every 10 to 14 days, which is part of why a burnt tongue recovers its sense of taste so quickly.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜的口味有点儿重。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de kǒuwèi yǒudiǎnr zhòng.
examples.english: This dish tastes a bit strong.

examples.hanzi: 冰淇淋有很多种口味。
examples.pinyin: Bīngqílín yǒu hěn duō zhǒng kǒuwèi.
examples.english: Ice cream comes in many flavors.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — 锻 is forging metal; also in 钱 money, 铁 iron.
段 (duàn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 缎 duàn (satin) and 煅 duàn.
火 (fire) — smelting and refining with fire; also in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp.
柬 (jiǎn) is only a loose clue; 炼 liàn sounds like 练 liàn (practice) and 链 liàn (chain).

example.hanzi: 坚持锻炼可以让身体更健康。
example.pinyin: jiānchí duànliàn kěyǐ ràng shēntǐ gèng jiànkāng.
example.english: Persisting in exercise can make the body healthier.
example.fact: Regular aerobic exercise has been shown to increase the volume of the hippocampus, a brain region central to memory, even in older adults. A 2011 study found that a year of moderate walking increased hippocampal volume by about 2%, effectively reversing one to two years of age-related shrinkage.

examples.hanzi: 他每天早上去公园锻炼。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān zǎoshang qù gōngyuán duànliàn.
examples.english: He exercises in the park every morning.

examples.hanzi: 这份工作能锻炼你的沟通能力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò néng duànliàn nǐ de gōutōng nénglì.
examples.english: This job can sharpen your communication skills.

meanings: (coll.) to be interested in (often used in the negative)

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
目 (eye) — a cap pulled over the eyes: to cover, to push ahead blindly. Used in 冒险 and 感冒.

example.hanzi: 他昨天淋雨后就感冒了。
example.pinyin: tā zuótiān lín yǔ hòu jiù gǎnmào le.
example.english: He caught a cold after getting caught in the rain yesterday.
example.fact: Over 200 different virus types can cause the common cold, with rhinoviruses responsible for the majority of cases. This enormous viral diversity is the main reason no universal cold vaccine has ever been developed, unlike for many single-pathogen diseases.

examples.hanzi: 我感冒了，嗓子很疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, sǎngzi hěn téng.
examples.english: I've caught a cold and my throat hurts.

examples.hanzi: 天气变冷，很多人感冒了。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì biàn lěng, hěn duō rén gǎnmào le.
examples.english: The weather turned cold and many people caught colds.

components.note: Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 他毕业以后在上海工作。
example.pinyin: Tā bìyè yǐhòu zài Shànghǎi gōngzuò.
example.english: After graduating he worked in Shanghai.
example.fact: 业 rarely stands alone; it builds 毕业 (to graduate), 职业 (occupation), 企业 (enterprise), 业余 (spare-time, amateur), and 作业 (homework). In Buddhism, 业 also translates karma.

examples.hanzi: 这是我这个学期的作业。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zhège xuéqī de zuòyè.
examples.english: This is my homework for this semester.

examples.hanzi: 你的职业是什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zhíyè shì shénme?
examples.english: What is your occupation?
